provenance.quote: Shall the City of Manhattan, Kansas be authorized to levy an additional one-half percent (0.5%) citywide general retailers' sales tax for street infrastructure maintenance pursuant to K.S.A. 12-187? Such tax shall take effect April 1, 2027, the day following the expiration of the existing special purpose citywide retailers’ sales tax which took effect April 1, 2017, or as soon thereafter as permitted by law, and shall expire 10 years later.

provenance.quote: Shall Unified School District No. 329, Wabaunsee County, Kansas (Wabaunsee), issue general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $14,000,000, to pay the costs to: (a) construct, furnish and equip a new career and technical education facility, including related site and infrastructure improvements; (b) make improvements and renovations to Wabaunsee Elementary School, Wabaunsee Junior High School and Wabaunsee High School facilities, including interior and exterior building, HVAC, window, fire alarm, safety and security, classroom and instructional space, roof, kitchen, playground and restroom improvements; (c) renovate and repurpose existing District facilities for administrative offices and educational programs; (d) remove existing modular facilities and undertake associated site improvements; (e) undertake all other necessary improvements related to the foregoing; and (f) pay costs of issuance and interest on the bonds during construction of the project; all pursuant to the provisions of K.S.A. 10-101 et seq ., K.S.A. 25-2018(f), K.S.A. 72-5457, and K.S.A. 72-5458 et seq .?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes a 0.5% citywide sales tax for street maintenance. It would begin April 1, 2027, after the existing special-purpose sales tax expires, or as soon afterward as the law allows, and would expire ten years after it starts.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the 0.5% street-maintenance sales tax for the stated ten-year period.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this proposed street-maintenance sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the school district to borrow up to $14 million through general-obligation bonds. The money could build and equip a career and technical education facility, improve the elementary, junior high and high school buildings, repurpose district facilities for offices and educational programs, and remove modular buildings. It could also pay related site work, bond-issuance costs and interest during construction.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $14 million in bonds for these school improvements and related costs.

In compliance with the provisions of K.S.A. 19-3424 and K.S.A. 25-105, notice is hereby given that a
general election will be held on the 3rd day of November 2026. The following candidates and positions
will be on the ballot:

Select from the drop-down menu below to view a list of candidates in the primary or general election for national and state offices in table format.  The table view of the  candidate list is updated automatically as each candidate files valid petition forms or declaration of intention forms.
Shall the following be adopted?
